name: Hardened Tortoise Shell
summary: Across the Shimmering Flats, racers seek shells tough enough for dangerous fuel. Gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway prize Hardened Tortoise Shells from sparkleshell tortoises because they resist volatile, corrosive experimental fuels.

sections.title: Natural Armor for High-Speed Hazards
sections.body: Sparkleshell tortoises, from snappers to borers, roam the salt flats. Their carapaces shield them from the salt and wandering predators. Gnomish experimental chemistry can corrode or rupture metal fuel tanks. So mechanics such as Wizzle Brassbolts prize the shells as raw material for makeshift tanks that resist acid and hold volatile rocket propellants.

faq.q: Where do you find Hardened Tortoise Shells?
faq.answer: Across the open salt expanses of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles, you can find Hardened Tortoise Shells on Sparkleshell Snappers, Borers, and common Sparkleshell Tortoises.

faq.q: Why does Wizzle Brassbolts want these shells?
faq.answer: Wizzle Brassbolts wants the shells for fuel tanks. Wizzle's brother is designing an extremely powerful, corrosive rocket fuel that threatens to melt their race car's chassis. Wizzle plans to hollow out and reinforce the durable carapaces.

faq.q: Can standard workshop tools easily shape them?
faq.answer: No. The carapaces are unnaturally hard. Gnomish mechanics expect to ruin a toolbox worth of metal implements carving, drilling, and shaping them into tanks.

angles.text: As an engineer, you can see why organic carapaces might suit high-pressure fuel tanks. When gnome-brewed fuel melts standard alloy piping, durable natural materials can take its place.
As a gnome, you might look at a desert tortoise and see a lightweight, resilient container for dangerous rocket fuel.
